drivingQuestion: Why may the finder claim the items belonged to the Amorites?
outcomeNote: Baraita limited to heavily rusted items

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנָא: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לוֹמַר לוֹ שֶׁל אֲמוֹרִיִּים הֵן. אַטּוּ אֱמוֹרִים מַצְנְעִי, יִשְׂרָאֵל לָא מַצְנְעִי? לָא צְרִיכָא
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The mishna teaches that if one found a lost item in a heap of rubble or in an old wall it belongs to him. The Sages «taught» in a baraita: It is his «due to» the fact «that» when the owner of the heap or wall claims the property, the finder «can say to him: They» belong «to the Amorites,» who lived in Eretz Yisrael before it was conquered by the Jews. The Gemara asks: «Is that to say» that «Amorites conceal» items but «Jews do not conceal» items? Perhaps it was the homeowner who placed the item in the wall or the heap. The Gemara answers: «No,» the baraita «is necessary» only in the specific case
«where» the item is «extremely rusted,» indicating that it had been left there for a long time.
